name: esVolta, LP
headquarters: Newport Beach, California (100 Bayview Circle, Suite 340); formerly Aliso Viejo; staff 'remote with periodic site travel' per the careers page
employees: Not stated; about 130 people named by department on the company's about page (September 2026); LinkedIn '51-200'; 28 staff at the July 2022 Generate acquisition per the Orange County Business Journal
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: esVolta is a Generate Capital-owned standalone-storage developer and owner whose sponsor has put it up for sale — Infralogic reported on 5 June 2026 that Generate 'has mandated Barclays and Truist as advisors for the sale of esVolta' and quoted Generate's CEO that the process 'has seen good interest' — while the company itself still describes itself as 'a portfolio company of Generate Capital' (June 2026 release). The premise handed to this dossier is right on two clauses and wrong on the third: esVolta is a mixed contracted-and-merchant owner in CAISO and ERCOT, but it has never named a PJM project; its stated markets are 'CAISO, ERCOT, WECC' with 'continued expansion into SPP and MISO'. The esVolta–Captona transaction of January 2025 was a USD 243 million preferred-equity investment plus ITC-transfer proceeds into three Texas projects, not a sale — esVolta remains the owner-operator. What the company says (June 2026): 'approximately 2.0 GWh' of operational and in-construction contracted storage, 'over 25 GWh' of pipeline across about 30 projects, 'Total Investment to Date: $1+ billion', founded 2017 by Randolph Mann, headquartered in Newport Beach, California. Operating as released: Anole 240 MW / 480 MWh (Seagoville, Dallas County; July 2025), Desert Willow 150 MW / 300 MWh (Midlothian; May 2025) and Burksol 100 MW / 200 MWh (Afton, Dickens County; March 2025) in ERCOT — 'a hedge in place with a confidential commodity market participant', otherwise merchant, on Sungrow PowerTitan systems with Saber Power and Quanta as EPCs; Hummingbird 75 MW / 300 MWh (San Jose; company says operating since March 2026) under a long-term PG&E resource-adequacy contract; Santa Paula 30 MW / 60 MWh (offtakers 'a major energy commodity firm and several California electric community choice aggregators'); Black Walnut 15 MW / 60 MWh (California Choice Energy Authority); Wildcat and Acorn (SCE, 2021). Under construction: Boxcar 150 MW / 300 MWh (Wylie, Texas; 'a long-term offtake agreement ... with a major corporate customer'; USD 139.6 million MUFG financing, COD 2027) and City Breeze 140 MW / 280 MWh (Bay City, Texas; groundbreaking April 2026). Financing since 2023: a USD 170 million First Citizens refinancing, a USD 185 million Nomura-led pre-NTP facility upsized to USD 450 million in June 2026 (CIP Green Credit Funds the largest lender), USD 258 million of ERCOT project facilities (MUFG, Nomura, KeyBanc, Investec, Cadence), USD 110 million Greenprint tax equity at Hummingbird, the USD 243 million Captona preferred equity, an ITC transfer to Computacenter at Black Walnut, and the MUFG Boxcar loan. Collection gap: Generate's stake, the acquisition price, any sale valuation, the hedge counterparty, the Boxcar offtaker and the ITC buyers in the Captona deal are undisclosed.
ecosystemRole: esVolta is the mixed-portfolio storage owner this corpus lacked: contracted resource-adequacy batteries in California, hedged-plus-merchant batteries in Texas, and a pipeline that runs into Arizona (Cactus Wren, 800 MW / 3,200 MWh, county-approved December 2025 with SRP 'in active discussions'), New Mexico (Gila Monster, 50 MW, for PNM), Colorado (Tava Mountain, 100 MW) and Montana. For a supplier it is a repeat buyer of Chinese integrated systems (Sungrow on all three Texas sites; Powin was its exclusive supplier through 2022) with a stated corporate facility earmarked for 'long-lead equipment procurement', and a sponsor-sale process that will decide who signs the next order. It sits with GridStor, Intersect Power and Nightpeak in Modo Energy's 'pure-play storage developers' group in ERCOT.

productsAndServices.name: Owned and operated storage — hedged-and-merchant in ERCOT
productsAndServices.description: Three operating projects totalling 490 MW / 980 MWh, all two-hour lithium-iron-phosphate systems: Burksol (100 MW / 200 MWh; Afton, Dickens County; interconnects through Wind Energy Transmission Texas; acquired from Highfield Energy in December 2022; commercial March 2025; EPC Saber Power), Desert Willow (150 MW / 300 MWh; Midlothian, Ellis County; commercial May 2025; EPC Saber Power; batteries 'from Sungrow' with 'liquid cooled HVAC' per the company's VP of Projects) and Anole (240 MW / 480 MWh; Seagoville, Dallas County, ERCOT North zone; commercial July 2025; EPC Quanta Infrastructure Solutions Group). Revenue model as the CEO described it to Utility Dive in January 2025: the projects 'have a hedge in place with a confidential commodity market participant. They will also participate in the ERCOT wholesale market.' The company put the trio at 'roughly 4% of ERCOT's anticipated 12.2 GW of storage capacity as of July 2025'. Financed by USD 258 million of construction, tax-equity bridge, letter-of-credit and term facilities (MUFG, Nomura and KeyBanc as coordinating lead arrangers, Investec, Cadence Bank; July 2024) and the USD 243 million Captona preferred equity plus ITC transfer (January 2025). ESS News reports Sungrow PowerTitan 1.0 on all three sites.
highlights: 490 MW / 980 MWh operating in ERCOT by July 2025; Modo Energy listed Anole ('247 MW | 480 MWh') among the largest Q3 2025 additions
The hedge counterparty has never been named; the balance is merchant — this is the contracted-and-merchant mix the brief describes
Preferred equity from Captona (with an unnamed equity partner) sits above the project debt; esVolta 'raised nearly $900 million for its energy storage business in 2024'
Modo groups esVolta with GridStor, Intersect Power and Nightpeak as 'pure-play storage developers (1.25 GW) ... scaling after proving models elsewhere' in its 2025 ERCOT report
productsAndServices.positioning: Merchant-with-a-hedge in Texas where GridStor tolls and swaps, Spearmint is fully merchant and Hunt Energy Network trades sub-10 MW units; larger than either specialist in ERCOT and smaller than Jupiter, Plus Power or Eolian.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wholesale energy and ancillary-services revenue plus a bilateral hedge with a commodity trader; tax credits monetised by transfer and tax equity

productsAndServices.name: Owned and operated storage — contracted in CAISO
productsAndServices.description: Hummingbird (75 MW / 300 MWh; San Jose, Santa Clara County; interconnected at PG&E's Metcalf 115 kV substation; selected by PG&E in July 2018 as one of four storage projects replacing gas capacity; 'long-term resource adequacy contract' with PG&E; USD 110 million tax equity from Greenprint Capital Management, November 2024; 'approximately 200 union jobs'; the company's projects page says 'Operating since March 2026' — no third-party COD article exists). Santa Paula (30 MW / 60 MWh; Ventura County, beside SCE's Wakefield substation; commercial January 2024; offtakers 'a major energy commodity firm and several California electric community choice aggregators'; U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance tax equity, 'esVolta's first tax equity transaction', November 2023; O&M by CAMS). Black Walnut (15 MW / 60 MWh; Santa Paula; selected by the California Choice Energy Authority in April 2020; commissioned October 2025; ITC transferred to Computacenter Holdings in December 2025, 'the first standalone ITC transfer by esVolta'). Wildcat (Palm Springs; 3 MW; operating since October 2021) and Acorn (Thousand Oaks; operating since April 2021) from SCE's 2017 IDER RFO. The 'esFaraday' California portfolio was refinanced at USD 170 million by First Citizens Bank in November 2023 (four projects, 370 MWh).
highlights: Hummingbird is the company's largest contracted asset and its only utility RA contract of scale; PG&E selected it in 2018 and it took until 2026 to operate per the company
The California book is small-project heavy: Santa Paula, Black Walnut, Wildcat and Acorn together are under 130 MWh
Counterparties are CCAs, a commodity firm and PG&E — the company has never named the CCAs beyond CalChoice's members
productsAndServices.positioning: A resource-adequacy seller to PG&E and CCAs, like Aypa's California book but far smaller; the contracts are what the corporate lenders underwrite alongside the Texas hedge.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term resource-adequacy contracts with PG&E and community choice aggregators; a bilateral contract with a commodity firm at Santa Paula
targetSegments: California community choice aggregators (CalChoice members Lancaster, Pico Rivera, Rancho Mirage, San Jacinto, Apple Valley per Energy-Storage.news)

productsAndServices.name: Development pipeline — 'about 30 projects, 25 GWh' across five markets
productsAndServices.category: Greenfield and acquired development (CAISO, ERCOT, WECC, SPP, MISO)
productsAndServices.description: Under construction: Boxcar (150 MW / 300 MWh; Wylie, Collin County; acquired from Black Mountain Energy Storage as 'Bufflehead' in March 2025; Oncor's Lavon 138 kV switching station; 'a long-term offtake agreement for the project with a major corporate customer'; USD 139.6 million MUFG construction, tax-equity bridge, letter-of-credit and term financing, March 2026; commercial 2027; filings cite Sungrow PowerTitan 2.0 as the design basis per Energy-Storage.news) and City Breeze (140 MW / 280 MWh; Bay City, Matagorda County; ERCOT queue 25INR0271 at 143.1 MW with an interconnection agreement and a projected COD of 18 March 2027; groundbreaking 9 April 2026 with Saber Power and SolaREIT) — together the 'Ironhorse portfolio', which brings the Texas book to 'five battery projects ... 1.56 GWh' by 2027. Permitted or in permitting: Cactus Wren (800 MW / 3,200 MWh, about 40 acres south of Maricopa, Pinal County, Arizona; Planning and Zoning 8–1 in November 2025 and Board of Supervisors unanimous on 10 December 2025; interconnection at SRP's Duke 500 kV substation; SRP 'in active discussions with the developer as we explore a potential energy storage agreement', ED3 requested pricing), Gila Monster (50 MW; Sandoval County, New Mexico; beside PNM's Rio Puerco switching substation; zoning approved 3–2 in August 2022; USD 300 million of industrial revenue bonds approved October 2024; construction 2027), Tava Mountain (100 MW; Colorado Springs; Planning Commission 6–1 in May 2025 to advance rezoning; Colorado Springs Utilities 'no current purchase plans'), Marmot Hills (250 MW) and Holly Oaks (125 MW) in California, and Beartooth (50 MW; Billings, Montana; NorthWestern Energy's 20-year pre-approval application was undone when a Montana court struck the pre-approval statute in May 2022). The June 2026 corporate facility is earmarked 'primarily to support project development, long-lead equipment procurement, and pre-construction costs'.
highlights: Cactus Wren would be the company's largest project by a factor of six; no offtake is signed and SRP's statement is the only utility interest on record
Boxcar's corporate offtaker is unnamed — the first corporate contract in the company's history per its own boilerplate ('supplying both utilities and corporate offtakers')
The pipeline figure has been stable at '25 GWh' since January 2025 while the operating book grew from 1.5 to 2.0 GWh
No PJM project has ever been named; 'Virginia' appears once, in the 2022 Generate release's list of development states
productsAndServices.positioning: A greenfield-plus-acquisition developer (Burksol from Highfield, Boxcar from Black Mountain) that keeps what it builds; Cleanview does not place it in its top 25 developers by pipeline.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Own balance sheet and project finance; no project sales reported
targetSegments: Arizona utilities (SRP, ED3) for Cactus Wren
productsAndServices.roadmap: Boxcar and City Breeze commercial in 2027; Cactus Wren groundbreaking targeted for 2026 per Energy-Storage.news; Gila Monster construction 2027 and 'full production' 2029 per the Rio Rancho Observer

productsAndServices.name: Corporate and project finance — the 'bankable' platform
productsAndServices.description: esVolta's own values list 'Bankable' and 'Fully Integrated'; the record is a sequence of facilities that grew with the fleet. Corporate: USD 185 million senior secured pre-NTP facility (April 2024; Nomura sole lead arranger and administrative agent; Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners Green Credit Fund I; Voya) — later described by the company as 'the $200 million facility originally closed in March 2024' — upsized to 'up to $450 million' on 3 June 2026 with Nomura leading, CIP Green Credit Funds I and II as 'largest lender', Allianz Global Investors, Celtic Bank, HSBC Asset Management, Fiera Infrastructure Private Debt and Truist Bank. Project level: USD 140 million esFaraday facility (February 2020; CIT lead; Siemens Financial Services, CoBank, KeyBanc) refinanced at USD 170 million by First Citizens Bank Energy Finance (November 2023); USD 258 million ERCOT facilities (July 2024); USD 139.6 million Boxcar (MUFG, March 2026). Tax credits: U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance tax equity at Santa Paula (November 2023), USD 110 million Greenprint tax equity at Hummingbird (November 2024) — Energy-Storage.news noted the release 'didn't make clear whether it was a conventional tax equity ... or a tax credit transfer' — the Captona preferred equity 'including ITC transfer proceeds' (January 2025) and the Black Walnut transfer to Computacenter (December 2025). Counsel throughout: Orrick for esVolta; Norton Rose Fulbright, Winston & Strawn and Kirkland & Ellis across the counterparties.
highlights: Nomura leads the corporate facility, as it does Strata's — the same bank desk finances both the originator and the owner in this corpus
CIP's credit funds are the largest corporate lender; CIP's equity fund is the buyer of Strata's Scatter Wash — the fund manager is on both sides of the Arizona storage market
'Total Investment to Date: $1+ billion' (homepage) against about USD 1.55 billion of disclosed facility sizes since 2020 — facilities are not draws
productsAndServices.positioning: A more heavily bank-financed platform than GridStor (whose sponsor is a bank) and a more sponsor-dependent one than Spearmint; the sponsor's own capital constraints are now the variable.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Corporate and project facilities arranged by Nomura, MUFG, First Citizens and KeyBanc; tax-credit monetisation by tax equity and transfer

relationships.note: esVolta's VP of Projects said Desert Willow's batteries are 'from Sungrow' with 'liquid cooled HVAC' (Midlothian Mirror, re-posted by esVolta); ESS News reports 'Sungrow PowerTitan 1.0 BESS batteries used across all three sites'; the Burksol groundbreaking notice lists 'Equipment suppliers: Sungrow and Fractal'.
relationships.context: Sungrow is the only battery supplier esVolta has named on an operating project since its Powin exclusivity ended in 2022. The company itself names Sungrow only for Desert Willow; the all-three attribution is trade press (ESS News) and a local notice (Texas Spur). Boxcar's filings cite Sungrow PowerTitan 2.0 as the design basis per Energy-Storage.news, but no supply agreement for Boxcar or City Breeze has been announced.

relationships.note: 'esVolta collaborated with ... Quanta Infrastructure Solutions Group at Anole on engineering, procurement, and construction' (company release, July 2025).
relationships.context: Quanta built the largest of the three Texas projects; Saber Power (not covered) built Desert Willow and Burksol and is the named partner at City Breeze. No Quanta role on Boxcar or City Breeze is reported.

relationships.note: Modo Energy groups esVolta with GridStor, Intersect Power and Nightpeak as 'pure-play storage developers (1.25 GW)' in ERCOT — 'scaling after proving models elsewhere'.
relationships.context: An analyst grouping, not a transaction. Both companies added ERCOT capacity in 2025 (Anole and GridStor's Hidden Lakes among the largest Q3 additions per Modo). GridStor tolls and swaps its output; esVolta hedges part of its Texas fleet and runs the rest merchant.

relationships.note: Intersect Power sits in the same Modo Energy 'pure-play storage developers' group as esVolta in ERCOT.
relationships.context: Analyst grouping only; no shared project or transaction is reported.

policyExposure.exposure: esVolta monetises the standalone-storage investment tax credit on every project it has financed since 2023: U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance tax equity at Santa Paula (November 2023, 'one of the first tax equity financings structured to capitalize on ... standalone energy storage under the Inflation Reduction Act'), USD 110 million Greenprint tax equity at Hummingbird (November 2024), ITC-transfer proceeds inside the USD 243 million Captona preferred-equity package for the Texas trio (January 2025), and a transfer to Computacenter Holdings at Black Walnut (December 2025). Its policy lead said in July 2025 that continued 'fair access to investment tax credits for energy storage' would keep the sector growing 'through 2033'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Tax-equity bridge loans are built into the MUFG-led project facilities (2024 ERCOT trio, 2026 Boxcar) so credits are monetised at or after COD.

policyExposure.exposure: The company has made no public statement on the foreign-entity-of-concern rules and its supplier code of conduct (revised February 2025) carries no FEOC or UFLPA language. The facts on record: its three operating Texas projects use Sungrow systems (a Chinese integrator) per the company's VP of Projects and ESS News, and Boxcar's filings cite Sungrow PowerTitan 2.0 as the design basis. periods.commentary: A sponsor-owned private company in a sale process: the numbers are facility sizes released by the company and its lenders, plus the company's own cumulative claims. No consensus or guidance exists, so 'expected' is empty throughout.

financials.commentary: About USD 1.55 billion of disclosed facilities since 2020 (corporate USD 450 million; project USD 170 million + 258 million + 139.6 million; tax equity and preferred USD 110 million + 243 million; plus undisclosed Santa Paula and Black Walnut credits). The corporate facility, upsized while the sponsor was selling, is the item that tells a reader lenders are underwriting the platform rather than the sponsor.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that esVolta is a mixed contracted-and-merchant owner in CAISO and ERCOT and not present in PJM — the brief's premise is two-thirds right. Basis: the company's own market list ('CAISO, ERCOT, WECC' plus expansion into 'SPP and MISO', June 2026), PG&E and CCA contracts in California, a hedge plus wholesale participation in Texas, and no PJM project in any source since 2017.

(High confidence) We assess that the January 2025 esVolta–Captona transaction was a financing, not a divestiture. Basis: the company's release ('preferred equity transaction structured by Captona LLC ... including ITC transfer proceeds'), Captona's own release ('joint venture'), and the July 2025 completion release naming esVolta as owner-operator with Captona as 'preferred equity' beside MUFG's debt. Renewable Energy World's 'acquires' headline overstated it.

(High confidence) We assess that Generate Capital is selling esVolta and that the outcome, not the current sponsor, decides the company's next three years of procurement. Basis: Infralogic's report of Barclays and Truist mandates and Generate's CEO on 'good interest' (June 2026), New Project Media's January 2026 report tying the process to Generate's own capital constraints, and the company's silence beyond 'portfolio company of Generate Capital'. Cutting against a distress reading: lenders upsized the corporate facility to USD 450 million during the process.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the hedge-plus-merchant Texas model is financeable because the credits and the corporate facility carry it, not because the hedge is large. Basis: USD 258 million of project debt was raised against 980 MWh of hedged-and-merchant batteries with a tax-equity bridge and a preferred-equity layer above it; the hedge counterparty, tenor and volume have never been disclosed, and Boxcar — the first project with a named contract type ('a major corporate customer') — was financed by a single bank at USD 139.6 million. A revenue-put or swap disclosure would strengthen this judgment; a lender release citing the hedge would weaken it.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Sungrow is the company's default integrator and that FEOC treatment of the 2026–2027 projects is the unaddressed risk. Basis: Sungrow on all three operating Texas sites (ESS News; the company names it at Desert Willow), Sungrow PowerTitan 2.0 as Boxcar's design basis (Energy-Storage.news), no FEOC language in the supplier code, and a corporate facility earmarked for 'long-lead equipment procurement'. No source states a supplier for Boxcar, City Breeze or Cactus Wren.

(Low confidence) We assess that Cactus Wren will be contracted with SRP or ED3 before construction. Basis: SRP's 'active discussions' and ED3's pricing request (January 2026) and a 2026 groundbreaking target; against it, no contract, no supplier and no financing eight months later, and an 800 MW single-site battery is six times the company's largest project.

Collection gap: Generate's stake and acquisition price, any sale valuation, the ERCOT hedge counterparty and terms, the Boxcar offtaker, the Santa Paula CCAs, the ITC buyers inside the Captona deal, the Black Walnut transfer amount, the Hummingbird commercial-operation confirmation from PG&E or CAISO, the employee count, and the board of esVolta LP are all unreported.

Indicators to watch: (1) a Generate release naming esVolta's buyer — an infrastructure fund or an IPP would settle whether the company stays a develop-and-own platform (Judgment 3); (2) a supplier announcement for Boxcar, City Breeze or Cactus Wren, and whether it is Sungrow again or a FEOC-compliant alternative (Judgment 5); (3) an SRP or ED3 contract for Cactus Wren and a groundbreaking in 2026 (Judgment 6); (4) Boxcar and City Breeze commercial operation in 2027 against the ERCOT queue's 18 March 2027 date for City Breeze; (5) the first named SPP or MISO project — the company has promised both markets since June 2026; (6) any disclosure of the Texas hedge's counterparty or tenor, or a revenue put on the merchant balance (Judgment 4).
